subject: Archaeology
title: The Book of the Dead
description: A quick, practical guide to The Book of the Dead.

hook.text: Egyptians buried their dead with an instruction manual for the afterlife. Getting it wrong meant oblivion.

buildup.text: The Book of the Dead contained nearly 200 spells to help the soul pass tests and avoid demons.

discovery.text: The final test was the Weighing of the Heart. Anubis weighed your heart against a feather of truth.

twist.text: If your heart was too heavy with sin, a monster called Ammit devoured it. No heart, no afterlife.

climax.text: Scribes mass-produced the scrolls with fill-in-the-blank names. Eternal life became a product you could buy.

punchline.text: Salvation had a price tag. Scribes sold afterlife insurance on papyrus.

quiz.question: What happened if a soul failed the Weighing of the Heart?
options: The soul was sent back to earth to live again
The monster Ammit devoured the heart, ending the afterlife
The gods assigned the soul to serve in the underworld forever

details.summary: The Book of the Dead is a collection of spells and illustrations placed in tombs to guide the deceased through the underworld. These papyrus scrolls described dangers, passwords, and the final judgment where the heart was weighed against the feather of truth.
details.whyItMatters: The Book of the Dead reveals Egyptian beliefs about death, morality, and cosmic justice. It shows that concerns about ethical judgment after death existed thousands of years before similar ideas appeared in other religions.
takeaways: Spells guided the dead through underworld dangers
The heart was weighed against Ma'at's feather of truth
Scrolls were customized and placed in individual tombs

faq.question: What happened during the weighing of the heart?
faq.answer: The deceased's heart was placed on a scale opposite the feather of Ma'at, goddess of truth. A heart lighter than the feather meant a virtuous life and entry to paradise. A heavy heart was devoured by the monster Ammit, destroying the soul forever.

faq.question: Was the Book of the Dead the same for everyone?
faq.answer: No. Scrolls were customized with the deceased's name and selected spells based on what the family could afford. Wealthy Egyptians had long, elaborately illustrated scrolls while poorer ones had shorter versions with fewer spells.
